title: e-Prescription Software India | Written to Dispensed | HIMS
meta: e-Prescription software for Indian hospitals and clinics: prescribe inside the consultation, choose from pharmacy stock, and dispense exactly what was typed.
h1: e-Prescription software where the prescription the doctor types is the one the pharmacy dispenses.
sub: HIMS lets a doctor prescribe from inside the consultation, choosing from the drugs the pharmacy actually holds. The prescription attaches to the patient record and appears in the dispensing queue, so nothing is read off handwriting.

hero_image.alt: HIMS pharmacy screen showing the dispensing queue with drugs, batch and stock

whatsapp_text: Hi, I'd like to see e-prescription and pharmacy dispensing in HIMS.
persona: Consultant, clinic owner or hospital pharmacist who wants prescriptions typed rather than written

paras: e-Prescription in HIMS means the doctor writes the drug order in the patient record during the consultation rather than on a pad. The drug is picked from a list drawn from the hospital pharmacy's own stock, with dose, frequency and duration recorded as fields. The prescription then sits on the encounter alongside the history, the examination and the investigations ordered at the same visit.

From there it moves by itself. The pharmacy sees the prescription in the dispensing queue, dispenses against what was typed and the issue drops the stock it came from. In the ward, the same order is what nursing works from when a dose is due. Nothing is transcribed at any point, which is where most prescription errors and most billing mismatches actually come from.

None of this needs the doctor to change how they consult. The prescription is written where the notes are already being written, and the rest of the movement, to the counter, to the ward and on to the bill, happens because every department is reading the same record.

items.q: Does the doctor prescribe from a drug master or from stock?
items.a: From the drugs the pharmacy holds. That is what stops a prescription being written for an item the counter cannot supply, and it is why the dispensing queue and the stock ledger agree afterwards.

items.q: Can we still print a prescription for the patient?
items.a: Yes. The prescription is printed from the record when the patient is buying outside, and it is also visible in the patient portal. The printed copy and the stored copy are the same document.

items.q: Is e-prescription available in clinics, not just hospitals?
items.a: Yes. Clinics and polyclinics use the same consultation and prescribing flow without the IP modules. See clinic management software for the smaller setup.

items.q: How does the pharmacy know a script has been written?
items.a: It appears in the dispensing queue against the patient, so the counter works from a list rather than from slips carried down by patients. Dispensing drops stock from the batch it was issued from.

items.q: Does this handle controlled or restricted drugs?
items.a: Prescriptions are recorded with the prescriber, the patient and the time, and pharmacy issues are tracked by batch, which is the record side. Any regulatory register your state requires should be discussed on the call so it is scoped correctly.

items.q: Is it part of the EMR?
items.a: Yes. The prescription is one of the things written on the clinical record, alongside history, orders and notes. See hospital EMR software for the record as a whole.

items.p: The whole hospital on one platform.
